slides.title: Displacement and Distance from Velocity
slides.lede: Opener: two scenes, six questions and a recap, answered on your boards

slides.title: The Toy Car, Reversed
slides.alt: A toy car on a straight track, drawn large

slides.eyebrow: The toy car, reversed · The situation
slides.title: A car described by its velocity

setup.preamble: This is the toy car from last lesson, but now we only know its velocity. The track shows the number line with the origin $O$, and the graph shows $v$ against $t$.
setup.para: At $t=0$ the car is at $O$. Its velocity is $v(t)=6-2t$ metres per second, for $0\le t\le 8$ seconds. As time runs, the area between the graph and the $t$-axis is shaded, and the readout under the graph gives the area. The car stays hidden until an answer is revealed.

facts.html: The car starts at $O$, so $s=0$ at $t=0$
Velocity $v(t)=6-2t$ in $\text{m s}^{-1}$, for $0\le t\le 8$ seconds
Area above the $t$-axis is shaded in one colour
Area below the $t$-axis is shaded in another

scene.alt: A toy car on a straight track above the graph of velocity against time, with the area under the graph shaded as time runs

slides.title: How far from O?
slides.stem: The car has run for $3$ seconds, and the shaded area so far is shown under the graph. Where is the car?

walk.cap: The shaded area is a triangle
walk.note: The base is $3$ s and the height is $v(0)=6\ \text{m s}^{-1}$.
The area under the $v$-$t$ graph is the change in position. The car is $9$ m to the right of $O$.

scene.alt: A toy car on a straight track above the graph of velocity against time, with the area under the graph shaded as time runs

slides.title: Position, distance, displacement (1 of 2)
slides.stem: From $t=3$ to $t=6$ the shaded area is below the axis. Where is the car, how far has it travelled, and what is its displacement?

walk.cap: The new area is a triangle below the axis
walk.note: Area below the $t$-axis counts as negative: the car is moving left.
The car is back at $O$.

scene.alt: A toy car on a straight track above the graph of velocity against time, with the area under the graph shaded as time runs

slides.title: Position, distance, displacement (2 of 2)
slides.stem: How far has the car travelled, and what is its displacement?

walk.note: Distance adds the sizes of the areas. Displacement adds the signed areas.

scene.alt: A toy car on a straight track above the graph of velocity against time, with the area under the graph shaded as time runs

slides.title: Total distance and position (1 of 2)
slides.stem: From $t=6$ to $t=8$ the shaded area is below the axis again. Where is the car now, and how far has it travelled in total?

walk.cap: The new area is a trapezoid below the axis
walk.note: The velocity goes from $-6$ to $-10\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ over $2$ s.
The car is $16$ m to the left of $O$.

scene.alt: A toy car on a straight track above the graph of velocity against time, with the area under the graph shaded as time runs

slides.title: Total distance and position (2 of 2)
slides.stem: Add the areas. What are the displacement and the distance in total?

walk.note: The signed areas add to the displacement. The sizes of the areas add to the distance.

scene.alt: A toy car on a straight track above the graph of velocity against time, with the area under the graph shaded as time runs

slides.title: Direction and the sign of the area
slides.stem: Watch the whole trip again, this time with the car shown. Look at which way it moves and which side of the axis the area is on.

walk.cap: The car moves right from $t=0$ to $t=3$
walk.note: The graph is above the $t$-axis, the shaded area is positive, and $s$ increases.

walk.cap: The car moves left from $t=3$ to $t=8$
walk.note: At $t=3$ the graph crosses the axis and the car turns round. Below the axis the area is negative, and $s$ decreases.

scene.alt: A toy car on a straight track above the graph of velocity against time, with the area under the graph shaded as time runs

slides.title: Michael's Ride
slides.alt: A cyclist on a hill, drawn large

slides.title: A ride described by his velocity

setup.preamble: This is Michael's ride from last lesson, but now we only know how fast he is going. The graph shows his velocity against time.
setup.para: Michael starts at home, so $s=0$ at $t=0$. His velocity is $v(t)=3.6t^2-60t+285$ metres per minute, for $0\le t\le 15$ minutes. The area under the graph is shaded as time runs. The hill and the rider stay hidden until an answer is revealed.

facts.html: He starts at home, so $s=0$ at $t=0$
Velocity $v(t)=3.6t^2-60t+285$ in $\text{m min}^{-1}$, for $0\le t\le 15$ minutes
The area under the graph is shaded as he rides
$s$ is the distance from home in metres, $t$ is in minutes

scene.alt: A cyclist on a hill above the graph of velocity against time, with the area under the graph shaded as time runs

slides.title: The first five minutes
slides.stem: Michael has ridden for $5$ minutes, and the shaded area so far is shown under the graph. How far has he ridden?

walk.note: The area under the $v$-$t$ graph is the change in position.
He starts at home, so this is also how far he has ridden.

scene.alt: A cyclist on a hill above the graph of velocity against time, with the area under the graph shaded as time runs

slides.title: The next ten minutes
slides.stem: Michael rides on to $t=15$. The area from $t=5$ to $t=15$ is shown under the graph. How far did he ride in those ten minutes?

walk.note: It is the change in position from $t=5$ to $t=15$, and he never turns round.
This is the average speed from the last lesson: the same $750$ m in $10$ minutes.

scene.alt: A cyclist on a hill above the graph of velocity against time, with the area under the graph shaded as time runs

slides.title: Home to the friend's house (1 of 2)
slides.stem: How far from home is Michael at $t=15$? Is that the same as the distance he rode?

walk.note: He starts at home, so $s(0)=0$.
$v$ is never zero, so he never turns round. The distance he rode and his distance from home agree.

scene.alt: A cyclist on a hill above the graph of velocity against time, with the area under the graph shaded as time runs

slides.title: Home to the friend's house (2 of 2)
slides.stem: What is the rule for finding the position from the velocity?

walk.note: Start position plus the signed area gives the position. Worked Example 1 in the notes starts here.

scene.alt: A cyclist on a hill above the graph of velocity against time, with the area under the graph shaded as time runs

slides.title: By Hand or by Calculator
slides.alt: The rule for position from velocity

slides.eyebrow: By hand or by calculator · Position
slides.title: Position from velocity, by hand (1 of 2)
slides.stem: We can find the position with algebra, not only by reading areas.

walk.note: Position is an antiderivative of velocity.
The car starts at $O$. So $s(t)=6t-t^2$.

slides.eyebrow: By hand or by calculator · Position
slides.title: Position from velocity, by hand (2 of 2)
slides.stem: Check $s(t)=6t-t^2$ against the positions we read from the areas.

walk.note: These match the areas: $9$ m right of $O$, back at $O$, $16$ m left of $O$.

slides.eyebrow: By hand or by calculator · Distance
slides.title: Distance by hand: split at the turning point (1 of 2)
slides.stem: How far does the car travel from $t=0$ to $t=8$? It turns round when $v=0$.

walk.note: $v>0$ before $t=3$ and $v<0$ after it.
The second is negative: the car moves left.

slides.eyebrow: By hand or by calculator · Distance
slides.title: Distance by hand: split at the turning point (2 of 2)
slides.stem: Now add the sizes of the two integrals.

walk.note: The signed integrals add to $-16$, the displacement.

slides.eyebrow: By hand or by calculator · Calculator
slides.title: Distance with the calculator (1 of 2)
slides.stem: A calculator finds the total distance in one go, with no splitting.

walk.note: $|v|$ flips the part below the axis above it.
RUN-MAT: OPTN, CALC, integral key. Abs is under OPTN, NUM. Type $6-2X$ inside it.

slides.eyebrow: By hand or by calculator · Calculator
slides.title: Distance with the calculator (2 of 2)
slides.stem: What does the integral of $v$ itself give?

walk.note: This is the displacement, not the distance.

slides.eyebrow: Recap · Displacement and distance from velocity
slides.title: Area under any velocity

cards: The change in displacement is the signed area.
The total distance is the area under $|v|$.
